title: Root rotation crash consistency across separate trust and minimum stores
mechanism_evidence: Root-trust history and trusted-root minimum remain separate durable SQLite stores.
Crash vectors use a distinct child process, parent-observed readiness, and external parent termination rather than injected exceptions or worker self-termination.
A durable newer root record with a stale trusted minimum is classified as ambiguous and is non-current for consequential use.

Recovery requires the exact authenticated next transition, exact root identity/public-key fingerprint, exact activation epoch, contiguous root epoch, and predecessor digest equal to the current trusted minimum.
Exact recovery replay is idempotent and does not create duplicate root records or duplicate minimum advancement.
Two independent recovery subprocesses racing the same exact ambiguous transition converge on the same root digest and trusted minimum binding.
A stale pre-rotation root snapshot cannot restore the prior root after the trusted minimum advances.
Clean R2-to-R3 rotation remains live after the crash/recovery cycle.
bounded_claim: On the tested same-host SQLite prototype, root rotation remained fail-closed across the preregistered genuine external-process termination boundaries surrounding the separate root-trust and trusted-minimum transactions. A durable newer root with a stale minimum was not accepted as current; exact authenticated reconciliation was idempotent under replay and concurrent recovery; stale-root restoration and semantic rebinding were denied; and a subsequent clean root rotation remained live.
not_proven: Physical power-loss or storage-controller reordering semantics.
Hardware fsync durability guarantees beyond the tested hosted SQLite environment.
KMS/HSM key nonextractability or hardware-backed root/minimum authority.
Separate operating-system privilege or administrative trust domains for the two authorities.
Security after compromise of both root-trust authentication material and trusted-minimum authority.
Atomicity across independent remote databases, KMS/HSM services, or geographically separate systems.
Production, release, deploy, or completion authority.
Universal correctness of model or reviewer conclusions.
hygiene_observation: Historical subprocess ResourceWarning messages from earlier Pilot 13/Pilot 14/Pilot 21 tests remain visible as inherited cleanup debt. Pilot 15's parent-kill helper explicitly closes its captured subprocess pipes after termination; the warnings are not treated as scientific endpoint success or failure.
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 16: isolate trusted-minimum advancement behind a separate platform-owned authority process and durable store so root signers, root-trust writers, registry writers, models, and reviewers cannot self-resolve an ambiguous rotation. Falsify forged, stale, replayed, rebound, unavailable, restarted, and concurrent recovery authorization while preserving exact-replay idempotency and clean R2-to-R3 liveness.
